summary: Iteration 10 — Tested 3 features end-to-end: (1) User email editing in Settings > Firm & Users, (2) Data-driven Reminders page with detail view, (3) Staff Billable Hours under Settings > Billable Hours. Backend: 14/14 pytest cases passed (email update + uniqueness + RBAC; reminders shape + sorting + scoping; billable hours POST/GET/DELETE/summary/export with partner-vs-staff RBAC). Frontend (partner Arjun): Reminders page loads 46 live items with filter chips, severity colors, type badges; detail view exposes Type, Status, Due Date, Assigned To, Client, Description, Priority and a working 'Back to Reminders' + Navigate button. Settings > Firm & Users edit-user modal exposes the new data-testid='user-email-input'. Settings > Billable Hours tab renders summary cards (Total Hours, Total Entries, Active Staff), filters (staff, client, date-from/to), view toggles (Time Entries / By Staff / By Client), Log Hours modal opens & creates an entry, By Staff and By Client cards render with per-row export buttons, and delete works. CSV export endpoint returns text/csv with attachment Content-Disposition.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~2410 lines — well past the 700-line guideline. Splitting into routers (auth, clients, tasks, engagements, billable_hours, reminders, exports) should be prioritised; this has been flagged in iter 9 as well.

Reminders endpoint sorts by (severity, due_date), but engagement reminders use `created_at[:10]` as due_date, which can artificially push them to the top of the list when an engagement was recently created. Consider using a separate sort key for engagements or omitting due_date on them.
Billable hours POST blindly trusts client-supplied client_name when present; consider always resolving the canonical name from db.clients to prevent inconsistent client labels in summary/export.

Reminders endpoint loads up to 200 tasks + 200 events + 100 engagements into memory and filters in Python; for larger firms this should move to a Mongo aggregation with date-range filter on the server side.
DELETE /api/billable-hours returns 200 with {'message': ...}; spec convention is 204 No Content. Minor.
Email uniqueness check is case-sensitive (find_one on raw email). Two users could be created with 'a@x.ae' and 'A@x.ae'. Consider normalising emails to lowercase on write.
